thread.title: Qualcomm Surges 7% as It Gives Up on NXP, Boosts Buybacks - Barron's

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Qualcomm Surges 7% as It Gives Up on NXP, Boosts Buybacks - Barron's
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated July 25, 2018 5:46 p.m. ET Qualcomm ( QCOM ) shares are up $3.83, or 7%, to $63.25, after the company said it would give up on a $52 billion bid to acquire NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ), and instead pursue up to $30 billion worth of stock buybacks.
Qualcomm also reported fiscal Q3 revenue and profit that topped analysts’ expectations, and forecast this quarter slightly higher as well.
"We intend to terminate our purchase agreement to acquire NXP when the agreement expires at the end of the day today, pending any new material developments,” said CEO Steve Mollenkopf .
"In addition, as previously indicated, upon termination of the agreement, we intend to pursue a stock-repurchase program of up to $30 billion to deliver significant value to our stockholders."
The NXP bid has been going on since October 2016. All the regulatory hurdles had been cleared except for China . Approvals this year appeared to fall victim to the posturing of the U.S. and China over tariffs and trade. Still, hopes had periodically risen in the last few months that Qualcomm would still get the deal done.
NXP will get a $2 billion breakup fee from Qualcomm. NXP shares are down $3.37, or 3.4%, to $95, in late trading.
Revenue in the three months ended June of $5.6 billion and EPS of $1.01 topped consensus estimates for revenue of $5.2 billion and EPS of 76 cents.
Qualcomm’s revenue from its “QCT” unit that sells chips directly to manufacturers of smartphones and such, rose by 1%, year-over-year, to $4.087 billion.
The “ QTL ” unit, which makes licensing fees and royalties, saw revenue rise 25% to $1.465 billion. That business has been engaged in an intellectual-property legal battle with Apple ( AAPL ) since early last year. The unit recorded no royalties from Apple’s devices during the period, as it has not for the past year, Qualcomm said.
For the current quarter, Qualcomm projects revenue of $5.1 billion to $5.9 billion, and EPS of 75 cents to 85 cents, on a non-GAAP basis.
That compares to consensus estimates for revenue of $5.47 billion and EPS of 77 cents.
